cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Prove We’re Close
cards.instruction: Get someone to take a social or emotional risk that demonstrates trust in the connection.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Before you send another 'fine,' tell me what you deleted. I want us to trust each other with the awkward version.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Let me be the person you can sound needy with.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You first. You always sound so casual.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I check whether you've replied before I get out of bed. Will you send me your needy bit now?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 demands the deleted version, but A3 let me and A5 will you are ordinary vulnerable requests after detachable status wording.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 needy fear prompts A3 safe-person offer; B4 reciprocity condition prompts A5 actual personal admission before renewed request.

relationship.evidence: B2 fears emotional exposure and B4 demands equal risk, directly changing A behavior.

heightening.evidence: B4 casualness challenge causes A5 a concrete morning-checking disclosure, not a generic claim of caring.

specificity.evidence: A1 fine versus deleted text establishes the private exchange; A5 bed/reply habit is a volunteered fictional fact.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 morning checking is earned by B4 challenge, but extra rank phrases do not produce an integrated tactic.
